Title: Credential stuffing leads to customer account takeover
Description: Credential stuffing against customer login leads to account takeover and use of saved payment tokens.
Existing Controls: Basic IP rate limiting at P1
Mitigations: M-01a: Breached-password screening at registration and login; M-01b: Per-account and per-IP rate limiting plus bot detection; M-01c: Offer passkeys/MFA; step-up auth on new device before paying with saved tokens
Verification: M-01a: Unit test against a known-breached password corpus; M-01b: Load test with credential-stuffing simulation; M-01c: Integration test for step-up on unrecognised device

Title: Forged PSP webhook marks unpaid orders as paid
Description: An attacker forges PSP webhook calls to P4. Only an IP allow-list protects the endpoint and signatures are not verified, so orders are marked paid without payment.
Mitigations: M-02a: Verify PSP HMAC signature over raw body with 5-minute timestamp tolerance; dedupe by event ID; M-02b: Verify payment status and amount via PSP API before fulfilment ("verify by fetch"); M-02c: Keep IP allow-list as defense in depth only
Verification: M-02a: Integration test - unsigned, mis-signed, stale and replayed webhooks return 401 and change no state; M-02b: Integration test - fulfilment blocked when PSP fetch disagrees with webhook; M-02c: Configuration review

Title: JWT validation accepts forged tokens
Description: JWT validation accepts algorithm switching or omits aud/iss checks, allowing forged tokens.
Mitigations: M-03a: Pin asymmetric algorithm; validate iss, aud, exp, nbf
Verification: M-03a: CI negative tests for alg:none and HS/RS confusion

Title: Client-supplied amount used to create PSP charge
Description: Client submits a manipulated amount or currency in the checkout request; P3 creates the PSP charge for the client-supplied amount.
Mitigations: M-04a: Compute amount server-side from cart and catalog; ignore client totals; M-04b: Reconcile captured amount against order total before fulfilment
Verification: M-04a: Abuse-case test with modified totals; M-04b: Reconciliation alert fires in staging on mismatch

Title: Refund race condition exceeds captured amount
Description: Concurrent refund requests (race condition) produce refunds exceeding the captured amount.
Mitigations: M-05a: Idempotency keys and transactional row locking on refunds; M-05b: DB constraint refunded_total <= captured_total
Verification: M-05a: Concurrency test issuing parallel refunds; M-05b: Migration test asserting constraint exists

Title: SQL injection in merchant order search
Description: SQL injection in the merchant order search modifies or exfiltrates records.
Mitigations: M-06a: Parameterized queries only; SAST rule blocking string-built SQL; M-06b: DB role for P6 without DDL or cross-tenant access
Verification: M-06a: SAST rule in CI; M-06b: Database grants review

Title: Fake payment events injected into the event queue
Description: A compromised internal workload publishes fake payment.succeeded events, triggering receipts and merchant fulfilment callbacks.
Mitigations: M-07a: Per-topic publish permission restricted to P3's identity; schema validation; M-07b: Consumers treat events as notifications and re-read authoritative state from DS1
Verification: M-07a: Broker ACL policy test; M-07b: Integration test with forged event

Title: Fraudulent merchant refunds cannot be attributed
Description: A merchant user issues fraudulent refunds and denies it; refunds are logged under P6's service identity, not the human actor.
Mitigations: M-08a: Propagate end-user identity (on-behalf-of token) to P3; audit actor, IP, session, device; M-08b: Dual approval above a refund threshold; notify merchant owners of refunds
Verification: M-08a: Audit log review of refund events; M-08b: Integration test for dual-approval workflow

Title: Audit logs deleted or altered to hide fraud
Description: An attacker with P3's cloud role deletes or alters audit logs to hide fraud.
Mitigations: M-09a: Producers have append-only permission; replicate to a separate security account with object lock (WORM); M-09b: Hash-chained log batches; alert on ingestion gaps
Verification: M-09a: Policy-as-code check on bucket policy and object lock; M-09b: Detection rule test

Title: Log injection forges or corrupts audit entries
Description: Customer-controlled fields containing newline characters forge or corrupt audit entries.
Mitigations: M-10a: Structured JSON logging with encoding; never concatenate raw input into log lines
Verification: M-10a: Unit test with CRLF payloads

Title: Cross-tenant BOLA on merchant transactions
Description: Merchant A reads merchant B's transactions by changing merchantId in /merchants/{merchantId}/transactions.
Mitigations: M-11a: Derive tenant from the token, not the path; centralized tenant-scoping middleware; M-11b: PostgreSQL row-level security as a second layer
Verification: M-11a: Automated cross-tenant authorization test suite in CI; M-11b: Database test asserting RLS policies

Title: PSP API key leaks
Description: The PSP API key leaks through logs, error dumps, environment inspection, or the CI pipeline.
Mitigations: M-12a: Fetch at runtime from DS4; restrict PSP key scopes and source IPs at the PSP; M-12b: Secret scanning in repo and CI; log redaction filters; M-12c: Rotation runbook and quarterly rotation
Verification: M-12a: PSP console configuration review; M-12b: Secret scanning enabled in CI; redaction unit test; M-12c: Rotation drill record

Title: Production snapshots expose PII in non-production
Description: Database snapshots are shared to, or restored in, non-production accounts, exposing customer PII.
Mitigations: M-13a: Masked synthetic data only in non-prod; snapshots encrypted with a key unavailable to non-prod; M-13b: Preventive guardrail policy blocking cross-account snapshot sharing
Verification: M-13a: KMS key policy review; M-13b: Policy-as-code test

Title: Stack traces returned to clients
Description: Stack traces and internal hostnames from P3 are returned to clients through the gateway.
Mitigations: M-14a: Gateway maps upstream errors to generic responses with a correlation ID
Verification: M-14a: DAST check for verbose errors

Title: SSRF via merchant callback URL
Description: A merchant sets their callback URL to an internal address or the cloud metadata endpoint; P5 fetches it and leaks credentials or reaches internal APIs.
Mitigations: M-15a: Egress proxy blocking private, link-local and metadata ranges after DNS resolution; M-15b: Enforce IMDSv2 with hop limit 1; isolate P5 network segment
Verification: M-15a: SSRF test suite against egress proxy (incl. DNS rebinding); M-15b: Infrastructure policy check

Title: Card-testing bots abuse checkout
Description: Card-testing bots use checkout to validate stolen cards at high volume, causing PSP fees, PSP account suspension risk, and degraded checkout.
Existing Controls: Basic IP rate limiting at P1
Mitigations: M-16a: Velocity limits per account, device, IP and card fingerprint; bot management; M-16b: PSP fraud scoring; alerting on authorization-decline ratio
Verification: M-16a: Load test with synthetic card-testing patterns; M-16b: Decline-ratio alert test

Title: Webhook endpoint flood or replay storm
Description: The webhook endpoint is flooded or bombarded with replays, backing up processing.
Mitigations: M-17a: Reject on signature failure first; rate limit; enqueue and process asynchronously; idempotent handlers
Verification: M-17a: Load test with replayed and unsigned webhooks

Title: PSP latency exhausts Payments Service workers
Description: PSP latency or outage exhausts P3 worker threads because charge calls are synchronous with no timeouts.
Mitigations: M-18a: Timeouts, circuit breaker and bulkhead for PSP calls; retry with idempotency keys; M-18b: Graceful "payment pending" UX
Verification: M-18a: Fault-injection test with slow PSP stub; M-18b: End-to-end test

Title: Ransomware or destructive attacker deletes DB and backups
Description: A destructive attacker or ransomware deletes the database and its backups.
Mitigations: M-19a: Deletion protection; point-in-time recovery; immutable backups in a separate account; M-19b: Quarterly restore drills with measured RTO/RPO
Verification: M-19a: Policy-as-code check; M-19b: Restore drill record

Title: Support role can call refund endpoints
Description: Merchant "support" role can call refund endpoints because function-level authorization is enforced only in the UI.
Existing Controls: UI hides refund button for support role
Mitigations: M-20a: Server-side policy engine with deny-by-default; permission matrix per endpoint under version control
Verification: M-20a: Authorization tests for every role-endpoint pair

Title: Payments Service compromise leads to cluster takeover
Description: Compromise of P3 leads to cluster takeover via a privileged pod and an automounted service account token with broad RBAC.
Mitigations: M-21a: Restricted Pod Security Standard; non-root, read-only root filesystem; disable token automount; M-21b: Minimal RBAC; default-deny network policies
Verification: M-21a: Admission policy test; M-21b: RBAC escalation-path analysis

Title: Malicious dependency exfiltrates PSP key
Description: A malicious dependency introduced via CI exfiltrates the PSP key at runtime. Detailed in TM-002.
Mitigations: M-22a: Hash pinning; dependency review; signed artifacts with provenance; M-22b: Egress allow-list for P3 (PSP and DB only)
Verification: M-22a: SLSA provenance verification at deploy; M-22b: Network policy test

Title: Friendly-fraud chargeback without sufficient evidence
Description: A customer disputes a legitimate purchase and OrbitPay has insufficient evidence for the chargeback.
Mitigations: M-23a: Retain 3-D Secure results, device and session evidence, delivery confirmation and receipts linked to the order
Verification: M-23a: Chargeback evidence pack review

Title: TLS verification disabled in PSP client
Description: TLS certificate verification is disabled in the PSP HTTP client (copied from a test configuration), enabling interception of charge requests and the API key.
Mitigations: M-24a: Enforce verification in a shared HTTP client library; lint rule banning verification bypass; M-24b: Egress through a TLS-validating proxy
Verification: M-24a: Lint rule in CI; M-24b: Network test with invalid certificate

Title: Customer PII over-collected in audit logs
Description: Found by the coverage check (README Section 11.7). Audit logs contain customer email addresses and IPs readable by a broad engineering group.
Mitigations: M-25a: Field-level minimization of audit events; restrict read access to DS3
Verification: M-25a: Log schema review; IAM access review
